chunks: From him, from Amr ibn Uthman, from al-Hasan ibn Mahbub, from al-Hasan ibn Salih al-Thawri, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) regarding:

A man who bequeathed to his slave one-third of his wealth. He said: The slave is appraised, then it is seen what the one-third of the deceased's estate amounts to. If the one-third is less than the value of the slave by the amount of a quarter of the value, the slave is freed for a quarter of his value. And if the one-third is more than the value of the slave, the slave is freed and what remains of the one-third after the value is paid to him.

key_terms.اسْتُسْعِيَ: Is freed by paying the difference

ai.seo_question: How is a bequeathed slave freed if the estate's one-third portion is less than the slave's value?
ai.summary: This ruling from al-Isfabar illustrates the Shia juristic principle of 'tadil' (appraisal) in testamentary bequests (wasiyya), ensuring the slave's freedom is funded directly from the one-third estate share rather than the heirs' portions. It highlights the practical application of the Quranic limit on bequests, balancing the testator's intent with the preservation of heirs' rights by adjusting the slave's manumission cost against the specific bequeathed amount.
